PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

SOLI · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

USD exposure: H1 report confirms approximately 30–35% of revenues denominated in USD (US operations: Custom Power, Q-Par, Active Silicon). H1 report states currency headwind of approximately £2.8m on revenues of £85.7m = ~3.3% headwind; avg rate $1.34:£1 in H1 vs $1.28:£1 prior year. The RNS today does not disclose a constant currency figure — Phase 0B override does not fire.

For the full year: USD exposure ~30–33% of revenues. GBP has strengthened vs USD over the year. The H1 rate of $1.34:£1 vs $1.28:£1 prior year = GBP stronger by ~$0.06, which is above the >$0.03 headwind threshold. Exposure band 30–35%.

Penalty: 🔴 [−8 pts] · ~32% USD · GBP headwind

Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~32% USD · GBP headwind

Note: the company naturally hedges a portion of this at the profit level (USD costs offset USD revenues), and the H1 report explicitly states "our natural hedge means the profit impact is substantially lower." The revenue-level headwind is real but EPS impact is diluted. I will apply the full −8 at Phase 5 but flag the partial natural hedge as a mitigant in the verdict.

PHASE 1 (CONTINUED) — FX LINE

  • FX: ~32% USD exposure · GBP/USD spot currently ~$1.29 (post-tariff USD weakness) vs H1 avg $1.34 → rate has partially reversed since H1. However for the full FY26 average, GBP was materially stronger than FY25's $1.28 average through most of the year. Net headwind confirmed for FY26. Phase 0B penalty: 🔴 [−8 pts] · GBP headwind · natural hedge mitigates EPS impact materially.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

SOLI · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (year ended 31 March 2026, results to be announced later)

1. Revenue Revenue expected to be "not less than £150m" and "ahead of consensus market expectations" for FY26. Consensus pre-RNS: £145.0m. Beat: +£5.0m minimum, +3.4% vs consensus. This is a floor figure — actual outturn likely £150–153m range given "strong year-end trading."

"revenue is expected to be ahead of consensus market expectations and not less than £150m"

2. EPS / Earnings Adjusted profit before tax "will accordingly also be ahead of consensus market expectations for FY25/26." Consensus adj PBT: £7.2m. No specific figure guided — qualitative upgrade only on PBT/EPS.

H1 actual adj PBT: £4.9m. Implied H2 adj PBT: must be >£2.3m (£7.2m − £4.9m) to meet consensus, and ahead of that to beat. H1 report indicated confidence in full year; H2 order book >60% of £87.3m = >£52m to ship, now £106.5m open book = very strong H2 coverage.

FY26e EPS bridge (FY27 implied):

  • FY26 base: adj EPS consensus 9.5p (57.1m shares diluted). If revenue beats to ~£150–152m, adj PBT likely £7.5–8.0m. At 25% tax → adj PAT ~£5.6–6.0m → adj EPS ~9.7–10.5p.
  • FY27 bridge from FY26 base of ~9.7–10.5p:
    • (1) New base EPS: ~9.7–10.5p
    • (2) Inorganic annualisation: no material acquisitions contributing partial-year in FY26 (Q-Par and Gateway both in from FY25 H2, fully annualised in FY26)
    • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: company targeting 20p EPS by 2030; FY27 consensus 10.5p already implies modest organic growth of ~10%. Order book £106.5m at year-end vs £97.0m at Nov-25 (£85.5m Nov-24) — growth trajectory intact. Power division $20m+ new orders in H2 represent meaningful FY27 revenue visibility.
    • (4) Interest step-up: net debt declining sharply; FY27fc £2.4m net debt, interest cover 10x — no interest headwind.
    • Implied FY27 EPS: 10.5–11.5p — stale FY27 consensus at 10.5p looks achievable to modestly beatable if FY26 beats materially. No large revision required to FY27 unless FY26 PBT beats by >£0.5m, which would pull FY27 base up.

3. Order book Open order book at 31 March 2026: £106.5m vs £97.0m at 30 November 2025 (+9.8%) and £87.3m at 30 September 2025. Primary driver: ~$20m of new Power division orders since the December update.

"The open orderbook as at 31 March 2026 of c.£106.5m (30 Nov 2025: £97.0m), has increased primarily as a result of strong order intake in the Power division since our December update, amounting to approximately $20m."

Order book as % of FY2 consensus revenue (£149.4m): 71.3% — exceptional forward coverage for a company of this type. Majority deliverable over next 18 months.

Also noted: initial order from new Communications customer announced in Q3, with shipments scheduled for Q1 26/27. This sits inside the £106.5m order book.

4. Divisional colour

  • Components: "strong year on year improvement benefitting from exciting new design wins in the UK and the US underpinned by improved market conditions." — cyclical recovery narrative confirmed.
  • Power: "significant improvement benefitting from the management re-organisation and investment in capabilities… strong demand from drone and other autonomous technology applications with significant new and emerging defence opportunities." — $20m order intake since December confirms this is real.
  • Systems: "continuing strong demand for communications products… building opportunities for antenna and integrated systems capabilities… growth opportunities not fully reflected in revenue in the period, they underpin the expected sales mix enhancement going forward." — CAIN programme (initial $10.8m order, deliveries in H1 FY27) plus communications pipeline.

"Components delivered strong year on year improvement benefitting from exciting new design wins in the UK and the US underpinned by improved market conditions."

"Power has seen significant improvement… strong demand from the drone and other autonomous technology applications with significant new and emerging defence opportunities."

5. Margin / profitability Adj PBT "ahead of consensus" — no specific figure. H1 adj operating margin was 6.5%. Company targeting >10% mid-term. No specific FY26 margin guidance given but PBT beat implies margin improvement vs H1.

Lead time extension noted: "In recent weeks lead times have started to extend significantly for certain components due to the demand arising from the adoption of AI and the impact of geopolitical instability." — this is a supply chain caution flag, not a margin warning. Framed as a management challenge, not a profit risk.

6. Capital / balance sheet No specific debt figure in today's RNS. H1 net debt £7.1m; FY1fc consensus £4.5m. H1 report guided cash generation H2-weighted, in line with expectations. New £15m RCF in place (post FY25 year-end), undrawn accordion of £10m.

DPS: FY1fc 2.5p (interim 0.92p already paid). No new dividend commentary.

7. Qualitative tone / outlook Chairman Rogers: "very well placed to fulfil the demand for sovereign technology and capability both in the UK and the US, and benefits from the resilience that is derived from our exposure to other structural growth markets."

Supply chain caution: "we are mindful of the macroeconomic effect of regional conflicts, and the resulting uncertainties on supply side constraints which are as yet unclear." — prudent language, not a downgrade signal.

EPS quality check: H1 FY26 adj EPS 6.5p vs reported diluted 5.0p. Effective tax rate H1 FY26: 25.0% (£963k on £3,848k PBT) — in line with standard rate. No tax distortion. No one-off credits inflating headline. ✅ Clean.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward language: "revenue is expected to be ahead of consensus market expectations and not less than £150m"; "adjusted profit before tax will accordingly also be ahead of consensus." Three brokers cited (Cavendish, Berenberg, Zeus) with consensus PBT £7.2m, Revenue £145.0m — both explicitly being beaten.

FY27 language: order book and divisional commentary provide structural optimism but no numeric FY27 guidance.

This is explicit beat language with "not less than" floor on revenue and PBT ahead confirmed. Classifies as:

🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit beat on both revenue (+3.4% minimum) and adj PBT vs three-broker consensus. "Not less than" language on revenue. All three divisions described as performing strongly. Order book record high.

Provisional points: +12 to +15

Divergence check: current year beat AND forward order book growing — no divergence. Beat quality row NOT required.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Today's RNS is an unambiguous full-year beat. Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers (Cavendish, Berenberg, Zeus) will move as follows: FY26 revenue raised by £5–8m to £150–153m; FY26 adj PBT raised by £0.3–0.8m to £7.5–8.0m; FY26 adj EPS raised by 0.2–0.5p to ~9.7–10.0p. Target prices will move from the current 247p consensus to a likely 270–310p range. The single watch-point is the AI-driven component lead-time extension — if this escalates, it could crystallise into a supply-chain risk in H1 FY27 as CAIN deliveries begin. **Received after scorecard produced.-

Broker note received. Per standing instruction, score does not change.

Key calibration observations vs CLBS score of 38:

Where the score held up well:

  • Cavendish cuts TP from 275p → 200p — consistent with the "hold/trim TP" call in the revisions cell
  • FY27e EPS direction: Cavendish cuts from a positive trajectory to −2.05c, worse than my −10 to −20% range assumption (actual cut is more severe: FY27e revenue flat at $23.5m vs my assumed $24–25.5m, and FY27 moves to adj. loss territory not just EPS trim)
  • Cautious tone confirmed — Cavendish explicitly frames this as a "12-month delay" derisking exercise

Where I was too optimistic:

  • I modelled FY27e as a recovery year toward profitability. Cavendish keeps FY27 in loss territory (adj. PBT −$1.4m, EPS −2.05c). FY28 is the first recovery year at 2.03c. My "−10 to −20% EPS cut" framing understated the severity — the actual outcome is FY27 remains loss-making, not merely trimmed profitable.
  • ARR miss vs Cavendish's own model was $15.0m vs $16.4mE — a larger shortfall than I had characterised. Critically, Cavendish flags ARR grew to $15.6m in H1 FY26 before contracting to $15.0m in H2. This H2 ARR contraction is more bearish than the net $15.0m figure alone implies — it means new business losses exceeded renewals in H2, which is qualitatively worse than the RNS headline suggested.
  • My scoring treated the Cautious outlook at −6 pts for qualitative-only guidance. The actual broker response (TP −27%, two forward years in loss, FY27 revenue flat not growing) suggests the correct penalty was closer to −8 to −10 pts on the forward guidance component. Score should probably have been 32–35, not 38.

The key miss in the Phase 2 analysis: The RNS stated ARR of $15.0m without disclosing the H1 peak of $15.6m. Cavendish had the H1 interim figure and can therefore identify H2 ARR contraction explicitly. From the RNS alone this was not derivable — it's a genuine information asymmetry that the workflow couldn't capture at scoring time.

The standing instruction holds — 38 remains the filed score. But the calibration lesson is clear: for subscription/ARR businesses, always attempt to triangulate whether H2 ARR momentum held vs H1, even when the RNS only discloses a year-end figure.

1. Revenue figures

Full year FY26 revenues expected to be approximately $23.3 million, described as "broadly in line with expectations." Consensus per RNS footnote: $24.1m. Actual vs consensus: −$0.8m, −3.3% miss. Prior year (FY25): $38.7m → YoY −39.8%.

6. Structural flags

Accounting transition: From 1 April 2025, CLBS introduced straight-line revenue recognition of future licence revenues and redefined cost of sales — this permanently alters reported revenue levels vs historical. The $38.7m → $23.3m decline is accounting-driven, not trading-driven.

ARR as primary metric: Under the recurring revenue rule (≥80% recurring with monthly recognition), ARR $15.0m is the primary coverage metric, not the IFRS 15 12-month backlog. #1 Driver — ARR trajectory and new business momentum. The $15.0m ARR (+10.3%) is the number brokers will focus on — it is the only clean metric unaffected by the accounting change. The miss vs expectations (new business underdelivery, Q4 deal slippage) is the primary negative driver. Brokers will compare ARR growth of 10.3% against whatever was modelled — the company's own statement that new business "underdelivered against expectations" signals ARR came in below internal targets even if it grew YoY.

#2 Driver — Revenue vs consensus slight miss, PBT slight beat. Revenue $23.3m vs $24.1m consensus = −3.3% miss. Adj. loss $0.2m vs consensus loss $0.3m = marginal beat. The beat is entirely cost-driven (H2 cost control) not revenue-driven. Brokers will note the asymmetry.

Forecast revisions: FY26 is already the final year — results due July 2026 will be the audited confirmation. The more important question is FY27 revisions. FY27e consensus: $26.9m revenue / 1.9p EPS. Given: (a) Q4 FY26 new business slippage into FY27; (b) ARR base of $15.0m vs FY27e revenue $26.9m implies ~$11.9m non-recurring/expansion revenue needed on top of ARR; (c) qualitative-only guidance with no numeric comfort. Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 278p. Current price 91.5p — already at a massive discount. Brokers unlikely to raise TP given the Q4 deal slippage revelation. Risk is downward TP revision if FY27 numbers are cut.

Conservative guidance read-through: No "not less than" or "comfortable with" language for FY27. The CEO statement is unusually candid about failure: "the end of the year saw several prospective deals, that were fully negotiated, being lost or suffering delays." This is anti-conservative guidance — it explicitly flags execution failure rather than providing comfort.

Key risk: Q4 FY26 deal slippage directly reduces FY27 opening pipeline quality. Deals that were "fully negotiated" and then lost are not recoverable — they represent permanent ARR misses. The statement that "several deals at contractual stage in Q4 were lost or further delayed" is the most bearish element of the RNS.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: CLBS guided FY26 revenue of $23.3m, a −3.3% miss vs consensus of $24.1m, and adjusted loss before tax of $0.2m, marginally better than the −$0.3m consensus. The single definitive catalyst is the Q4 new business failure — several deals that were "fully negotiated" were lost or delayed, delivering ARR of $15.0m (+10.3%) against what the company itself acknowledges was below its own expectations. The revenue and ARR miss combination confirms that the accounting transition narrative (used to explain the $38.7m → $23.3m revenue collapse) cannot fully offset the operational shortfall in new logo acquisition.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the implied H2 metric dominates. Implied H2 revenue of $13.0m is −39.5% YoY vs FY25 H2 $21.5m — classified 🔴 severe. The company explicitly attributes this to the accounting change, and the ARR growth of 10.3% confirms underlying retention is intact. However, the downside risk to the upgrade cycle is real: Q4 deal slippage means FY27 opens with a weaker pipeline than the December 2025 consensus assumed. The 97.6% NRR is the bear-case floor — brokers will anchor on this as evidence the installed base is sticky, limiting downside to existing revenue. The structural floor is the ARR base of $15.0m, which covers 55.8% of FY27e consensus revenue.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 is effectively confirmed — results due July. The revision pressure falls entirely on FY27e. Revenue consensus $26.9m faces a −5 to −10% cut risk given Q4 pipeline slippage; EPS consensus 1.9p faces a −10 to −20% cut risk given operating leverage on a near-breakeven P&L. TP of 278p is unlikely to be raised — possible modest trim to 240–260p range. The stock at 91.5p already prices in significant disappointment (67% discount to TP), but the Q4 deal disclosure removes a near-term re-rating catalyst. 


🏁 Score 38/100 — Cautious: broker revisions likely modestly negative on FY27, TP held or trimmed; Q4 deal slippage is the key overhang on any near-term recovery thesis.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 December 2025). Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Sharescope has not yet rolled forward to 31/12/26 — consistent with the rule that Sharescope does not roll until FY results are published. So FY1 = FY25 (the year just reported), FY2 = FY26 (the current live year).

Five explicit row label mappings:

  • Next year end 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25
  • FY1 − 1 = FY24 (1y ago)
  • FY1 − 2 = FY23 (2y ago)
  • FY1 − 3 = FY22 (3y ago)

PHASE 0B — FX CHECK — DEVO

DEVO reports in USD. Sharescope Currency: USD. Revenues are earned via third-party distribution platforms (Steam, consoles) — global revenues, no single geographic disclosure provided per Note 2 of accounts: "The Group does not provide any information on the geographical breakdown of revenues." No Currency Movements section in RNS. Cannot identify single non-GBP currency >30% from RNS. No Phase 0B penalty applicable. No FX badge.

PHASE 1 — DEVO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +13.3% (1.5p → 1.7p). Momentum 🟢 RISING — gradual upward drift over the period, with one small upgrade step in August 2025 (1.5p → 1.6p) and further drift to 1.7p. Revenue net change: $112.5m → $106.0m = −5.8%. Revenue consensus has drifted down while EPS has risen — reflects improving margin expectations.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 45.4% × $106.0m = $48.1m · EPS: H1 avg split n/a (historical H1 EPS all negative in a loss-making company)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue $51.6m · EPS −1.0p (H1 loss)

EPS: FY25 reported adj. diluted EPS −1.0p (in pence). Sharescope FY1 fc = 1.7p. The Zeus broker note confirms adj. diluted EPS (p) FY25A = −1.0p. Sharescope FY1 fc 1.7p was pre-results consensus — the actual delivered −1.0p vs 1.7p forecast. However, Zeus note shows FY26E EPS = 1.8p (their above-consensus figure). This requires careful treatment — see Phase 2.

PHASE 2 — DEVO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue

FY25 actual revenue: $107.9m, +3.0% YoY (FY24: $104.8m). vs Sharescope FY1 consensus $106.0m → +$1.9m, +1.8% beat. vs Zeus estimate $107.5m → essentially in line (+0.4%).

"Revenue performance was in line with guidance given at the start of the year, rising 3.0% year-on-year to US$107.9 million."

2. EPS / Adjusted EBITDA

Adjusted EBITDA (post impairments): $7.1m (FY24: $5.1m), +39.4% YoY. vs Sharescope FY1fc EBITDA $10.5m → miss on Sharescope consensus. vs Zeus estimate $7.0m → in line (+1.4%). Note: the Sharescope EBITDA fc $10.5m likely embeds impairments-excluded definition vs Zeus using post-impairment. This discrepancy is definitional.

Adj. diluted EPS (pence): FY25A = −1.0p (Zeus note). Sharescope FY1 fc was 1.7p. This is a large apparent miss. However: the Zeus note adj. EPS definition = post non-cash impairments of released titles, pre share-based payments. The statutory EPS is −$0.034 (−2.6p approx). The difference between the 1.7p Sharescope forecast and the −1.0p actual is driven by: (1) the $4.3m non-cash performance impairment; (2) the $14.6m non-cash deferred tax write-down. The DTA write-down is entirely non-cash and non-recurring — it does not affect adj. EBITDA.

EPS quality check: The statutory net loss of $16.0m is dominated by a non-cash DTA write-down of $14.6m. This is a one-off non-cash item with zero operational significance. Adj. EBITDA of $7.1m and positive FCF in H2 are the relevant operating metrics. The effective tax charge (statutory) was $13.4m on PBT of −$2.6m — this is entirely the DTA write-down. Restating adj. EPS on an operating basis (pre DTA write-down): adj. PBT = $7.3m (from Zeus note) × ~20% tax = ~$5.8m PAT / 474.5m shares = ~$0.012 = ~0.9p. Sharescope consensus 1.7p vs actual ~0.9p adj. = still a miss, driven primarily by the $4.3m impairment charge flowing through to adj. EBITDA post-impairment. 🚨 Impairment-driven EPS shortfall vs Sharescope consensus: headline adj. EPS ~−1.0p vs 1.7p fc; difference = $4.3m impairment + share count dilution. Impairments are non-cash but broker-visible.

FY26e EPS bridge (constructed here, referenced in Phase 4): (1) New base: FY25 adj. EBITDA (post impairments) = $7.1m. (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: nil in FY25 — no acquisitions (Zeus notes $5.6m acquisition assumed in FY26E). (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: RNS guides "continued revenue and Adjusted EBITDA growth in 2026." Zeus models FY26E adj. EBITDA = $14.6m. The organic driver: 15+ new releases in H1-weighted schedule, STARSEEKER release in June, Steam Publisher Sale. Revenue consensus FY26e = $115.5m (+7.1% organic growth). Applying similar EBITDA margin improvement (from 6.6% to ~11.8% per Zeus) = incremental EBITDA ~$7.5m. (4) Interest step-up: nil — net cash company, no debt drawdown. Finance costs FY25 = $0.16m. Implied FY26e adj. EBITDA: ~$14–15m. EPS: $14.6m EBITDA − $0.2m depreciation − tax ~$2.9m = ~$11.5m PAT / 484m diluted shares = $0.024 = ~1.8p. Bridge-implied FY26e EPS: ~1.8p vs Sharescope FY2 fc 2.3p → bridge supports Zeus (1.8p) but suggests Sharescope consensus (2.3p) is optimistic by ~25%. Risk of FY26 consensus cut from 2.3p toward 1.8–2.0p range.

3. Order book / pipeline

Pipeline: at least 13 new titles in FY26, including STARSEEKER: Astroneer Expeditions, Serious Sam: Shatterverse, and several lower-cost third-party releases. Over 30 titles in pipeline for next three years.

"Pipeline of at least 13 new titles in FY26 with greater visibility and control over our release cadence."

Front catalogue revenues: $37.9m (+218% YoY from $11.9m). Back catalogue: $68.9m (−24% YoY from $91.1m but improving in H2 vs H1's −38%).

4. Margin / profitability

Gross margin: 30.7% (FY24: 28.7%) — +200bps expansion. Driven by 11% reduction in marketing costs and 24% decline in game development expenditure. Adj. operating expenses −1.1% YoY to $26.5m.

"Gross margins expanded to 30.7%, up from 28.7% in 2024, primarily due to an 11% reduction in marketing costs, and a 24% decline in game development expenditure."

FY26 guidance: "significantly first half weighted" due to platform deals, Steam Publisher Sale, and release cadence. EBITDA expected to grow.

5. Capital / cash

Cash: $36.6m at 31 Dec 2025 (FY24: $41.6m). Positive FCF in H2 2025. No borrowings. Company expects positive FCF continuation through 2026.

6. Qualitative tone

Strong 2026 start: January — three titles in Steam Global Best Sellers Top 10 (Devolver's first). BALL x PIT content updates + console/mobile launch. Quarantine Zone: The Last Check performing strongly.

"Positive start in January 2026 with Quarantine Zone: The Last Check performing strongly in the weeks after release and three titles in Steam Global Best Sellers Top 10 list, a Devolver 'first'."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 guidance: "Expect to deliver continued revenue and Adjusted EBITDA growth in 2026." H1-weighted release schedule. "Significantly stronger" H1 than H2. Strong start confirmed. CEO statement: "excited about the opportunities for continued progress in the year ahead."

Language is constructive with a specific H1-weighting qualifier and strong January trading evidence. Not "not less than" but directionally positive with visible catalysts (STARSEEKER release, Steam Publisher Sale).

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — "comfortable" equivalent language with visible earnings drivers, confirmed strong start, H1-biased release schedule already partially confirmed. Provisional points: +6 to +10.

  • FY1 − 3 = FY23 (3y ago)
  • FY2 = FY27

⚠️ Sharescope EPS H2 field glitch confirmed: All historical H1+H2 EPS sums are zero or negative vs positive FY actuals — classic Sharescope glitch where H2 EPS = negative of H1 (i.e. H2 field = −H1, making H1+H2 = 0 or near-zero). Derive H2 EPS as FY actual minus H1 actual throughout.

Correct derivations:

  • FY23: H1 1.7p + H2 actual = FY 2.2p → H2 = 0.5p (not −1.7p)
  • FY24: H1 2.5p + H2 actual = FY 9.6p → H2 = 7.1p (not −2.5p)
  • FY25: H1 2.9p + H2 actual = FY 6.5p → H2 = 3.6p (not −2.9p)

Revenue H2 cross-check: FY23 H1 $6.1m + H2 $6.0m = $12.1m ✓. FY24 H1 $7.0m + H2 $13.0m = $20.0m ✓. FY25 H1 $8.5m + H2 $9.2m = $17.7m ✓. Revenue fields clean.

PHASE 0B — FX CHECK — IGP

Sharescope Currency: GBP. RNS reports revenues in GBP with some USD contract values disclosed. Revenues are GBP-denominated for Sharescope purposes. The RNS announces new orders/renewals in USD ($5.22m aggregate) — this is USD contract value for a GBP-reporting entity. Revenue from US government clients represents a significant portion of the business (US Federal Government is named as a major client; US revenue clearly >30% of total). However, the RNS does not contain a Currency Movements section with prior-year average rate comparison. The Cavendish broker note shows all revenue in GBP and does not flag FX as a material item. On constant currency basis: the RNS states revenues declined 0.5% on constant currency basis vs 2.8% reported decline. GBP/USD rate movement has caused a headwind of ~2.3% on revenues.

Phase 0B gate: Revenue in single non-GBP currency. USD revenues exceed 30%? Given the US Federal Government client alone renews at ~$3.5m = ~£2.8m of a £17.2m total = ~16%. However aggregate US-sourced revenue is likely higher (multiple US clients). Without explicit disclosure of % breakdown, cannot confirm >30% with certainty. The constant currency disclosure shows GBP/USD headwind translated ~2.3pp of revenue decline. Applying the Constant currency override test: reported −2.8% vs constant currency −0.5% → difference is 2.3pp, NOT within 0.5pp → override does NOT fire.

Given: (a) US revenues likely 40–50%+ of total for a company whose primary market is US Federal Government; (b) GBP strengthening caused 2.3pp headwind; (c) no explicit prior-year average rate in RNS. Apply Missing baseline fallback: mid-point penalty for likely 40–50% USD exposure, GBP headwind direction confirmed by cc vs reported gap.

Penalty: 40–50% exposure, headwind → −10 pts mid-point. Widen confidence ±5pp. Note: no prior average rate available.

"a large US Federal Government annual subscription renewal for MyID CMS, totalling c$3.49m with a longstanding US client for the period from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027."

Recurring revenues (support, maintenance, subscriptions): approximately £11.4m = ~66% of total revenues. Subscription revenue: £2.0m (+17.6% YoY) from £1.7m.

"Recurring revenues from support & maintenance, and subscriptions amounted to approximately £11.4m, representing c66% of total revenues."

ARR coverage rule consideration: Recurring revenue is ~66%, not ≥80%. The business is not yet fully subscription-based. The ARR rule does not fully apply — backlog/renewal pipeline remains the relevant visibility metric. However, the £2.0m subscription revenue growing +17.6% is the directional positive.

Year-end gross cash: £20.0m (FY25: £18.7m). Ahead of Cavendish forecast £19.6m. Debt-free.

"As at 31 March 2026, the Group held gross cash balances of £20.0m (2025: £18.7m)."

6. Qualitative tone

Revenue headwinds: procurement delays (US Federal), geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East). CEO: "encouraged by customer engagement and the improvement in order intake momentum in the second half of FY26." FY27 entry: "well placed to build on this momentum, while being mindful of the evolving global macroeconomic environment."

"As we enter the new financial year (FY27), the Group is well placed to build on this momentum, while being mindful of the evolving global macroeconomic environment."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY27 guidance: qualitative only. No numeric comfort on £21.0m consensus. "Well placed to build on momentum" hedged by "mindful of evolving global macroeconomic environment." H2 FY26 order intake improvement is positive. But: US Federal procurement delays remain a risk (geopolitical/macro); no explicit comfort with £21.0m consensus which requires +22% revenue growth. The $5.22m of announced orders includes FY27 commitments — the $3.49m renewal is for FY27 = 16.6% of £21.0m consensus already secured. PHASE 2 — AO.

AO. · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update — full year to 31 March 2026.

1. Revenue

Total group revenue growth expected to be c.11%. B2C growth c.9.5%.

FY1 consensus: £1,257.8m. Prior-year FY25 actual: £1,137.6m. Implied FY26 actual: £1,137.6m × 1.11 = £1,262.7m. Beat vs consensus: +£4.9m / +0.4% — essentially in line, marginally ahead.

"Total Group revenue growth expected to be c. 11%."

2. EPS / Earnings

Adjusted PBT "at the top end of £45–£50m". Midpoint guidance top-end = £50m. Prior FY1 fc consensus PBT: £49.8m. RNS confirms at top end → beat vs consensus PBT of approximately +0.4% (£50m vs £49.8m).

RNS states "c.15% year-on-year adjusted PBT growth". Prior year H1+H2 PBT: £17.1m + £11.6m = £28.7m. 15% growth → ~£33.0m. Wait — FY25 actual Sharescope: H1 £17.1m + H2 £11.6m = £28.7m. 15% on £28.7m = £33.0m. That contradicts "top end of £45–£50m". Reconciliation: the c.15% must reference a different base. FY25 PBT was £28.7m per Sharescope but consensus FY1 fc was £49.8m — implying prior-year actual reported elsewhere. The FY25 annual report data in the IPX block doesn't apply. Resolution: FY25 adjusted PBT not directly stated for AO in data block. The guidance "c.15% YoY growth" and "top end of £45-£50m" imply prior year adjusted PBT ~£43.5m (£50m ÷ 1.15). Sharescope's H1+H2 PBT sum of £28.7m likely reflects IFRS PBT, not adjusted. Taking the RNS guidance at face value: adjusted PBT ~£50m at top end vs FY1 fc consensus £49.8m → marginal beat, effectively in line at top end of guided range.

"Adjusted profit before tax is expected to be in line with previously upgraded guidance; at the top end of £45-£50m. Demonstrating again that profits are growing quicker than sales, in the region of c15% year-on-year adjusted PBT growth."

FY26e EPS bridge (for FY27e):

  • New base: FY26 adj PBT ~£50m. Tax at ~25% = £37.5m PAT. Diluted shares 555.6m → implied FY26 adj EPS ~6.75p. (Note: FY1 fc consensus 6.3p — the bridge will reference this base.)
  • (1) New base EPS: ~6.75p (RNS-derived, slightly above consensus 6.3p given top-end PBT guidance)
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: No acquisitions disclosed — nil
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY2 fc EBITDA £86.3m vs FY1 fc £79.3m = +8.8% organic growth. Applying to ~£50m PBT → ~£54.4m PBT. Tax 25% → £40.8m → ~7.34p EPS
  • (4) Interest step-up delta: Net debt virtually nil (FY1fc £4.3m, ND/EBITDA 0.05x); finance costs immaterial. No drawdown >£50m, no >15% finance cost growth. Mandatory row does not fire.
  • Implied FY27e EPS: ~7.3p. vs FY2 fc consensus 7.1p → +3% vs stale consensus. Bridge suggests consensus marginally stale to the upside given top-end FY26 delivery.

3. Order book / forward work

Not applicable (retailer). Membership model and "shared economics strategy" referenced. "Exciting pipeline of new initiatives ahead."

4. Margin / profitability

Adjusted PBT growing faster than sales ("profits are growing quicker than sales"). Hedging in place: ~80% of forecast fuel usage and 100% of electricity usage for full FY27 trading period — explicit forward cost protection.

"The Group had hedging arrangements in place in advance of recent geopolitical developments, covering approximately 80% of forecast fuel usage and 100% of electricity usage which cover the full FY27 trading period."

5. Capital returns / per-share / cash

Free cash flow c.£65m FY26 (FY25: £23m) — +£42m YoY, +183%. Liquidity c.£200m at period end.

"At the period end we expect to have c. £200m of liquidity. Profit is converting to cash, with free cash flow of c.£65m (FY25 £23m) for FY26."

No dividend. No buyback disclosed.

6. Qualitative tone

CEO language strongly positive. "The numbers speak for themselves again." Trust milestone (1 million Trustpilot reviews at 4.9 rating). "All key metrics continue to improve, with an exciting pipeline of new initiatives ahead."

EPS quality check: No exceptional items in FY26 per RNS ("There are no adjusting items in FY26"). FY25 had Music Magpie acquisition costs (£3.3m) and mobile goodwill impairment (£19.5m) — both excluded from adjusted. No tax distortion flagged. Headline adjusted PBT figure is clean. ✅ No restatement required.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements for FY27:

  • Hedging covering 80% fuel + 100% electricity for full FY27 period — explicit cost protection against geopolitical headwinds
  • "Exciting pipeline of new initiatives ahead"
  • "All key metrics continue to improve"
  • No numeric FY27 EPS or revenue guidance given
  • Management tone is bullish qualitative with specific cost hedge detail

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — confident qualitative language with concrete FY27 cost hedge, visible earnings driver (FCF step-up), ongoing market share gains. Not "upgrade-triggering" as no "ahead of" language for FY27 specifically, and no numeric uplift stated.

Guidance: qualitative only · covers one year ahead implicitly (FY27) · provisional points: +7 to +9

Divergence check: Current year delivery strong (PBT top end, FCF +183%). Outlook constructive. No divergence — both directionally positive. No flag required.

PHASE 2 — IPX

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update — Q2 AUM update for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 (H1 FY26 mid-point; this is the second quarter of IPX's financial year).

1. Revenue figures

Management guides FY26 revenue to be "in the region of £109m–£113m". Midpoint: £111m. FY1 fc consensus: £123.9m. Miss vs consensus: −£12.9m / −10.4% at midpoint.

Prior-year FY25 revenue: £141.9m. Guided range implies YoY decline of −22% to −25%.

"We expect that our revenue for the financial year will be in the region of £109m - £113m."

This is a material explicit downgrade to consensus. No H1 revenue figure disclosed.

2. EPS / Earnings

No EPS guidance in this RNS. Revenue guidance range of £109–113m vs consensus £123.9m = −10.4% miss on revenue midpoint. Operating leverage is high (adjusted operating margin 23.7% in FY25). A 10% revenue cut will translate to a significantly larger % EPS cut.

EPS impact estimate: FY25 adj op costs £108.2m on £141.9m revenue. Fixed cost base is substantial (staff costs £71.5m even after redundancies). Running a rough drop-through: variable component of costs ~35–40%. Fixed cost base ~£65–70m. On revenue of £111m, contribution ~£111m × (1 − 0.65) = ~£38.8m gross contribution vs fixed cost ~£65m → adj OP ~negative. This looks alarming. Revisit: FY25 adj op margin 23.7% on £141.9m = £33.6m. On £111m revenue at same cost base, adj op ≈ £111m × ~30% assumed variable cost pass-through...

More carefully: FY25 adj costs £108.2m = staff £71.5m + other £36.7m. Staff is partly variable (bonuses linked to profit). Management cut headcount and costs. If revenue falls to £111m (−22%), and costs fall proportionately: FY25 adj cost ratio 76.3%. On £111m with cost savings, assume 78–80% cost ratio (some fixed cost dilution) → adj OP £111m × 22% = £24.4m → adj PBT ~£25m → tax 25% → PAT ~£18.8m ÷ 128m diluted shares = ~14.7p adjusted EPS. FY1 fc consensus currently 18.3p. Implied cut: approximately −19 to −22% on current consensus. This is a severe downgrade.

FY27e EPS bridge:

  • (1) New base EPS: ~14–15p (RNS-derived revenue guidance floor)
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: SKY Harbor acquired April 2025; will be fully annualised in FY26. Contributes ~£3.5m full-year revenue per accounts (vs £1.7m in H2 FY25). Net additional delta in FY27: minimal as SKY will already be in FY26 run-rate.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: FY2 fc EBITDA £34.5m vs FY1 fc £29.6m = +16.5%. But FY1 fc is now ~£24m adj OP (revised). FY27 would need significant AUM recovery to get to £34.5m EBITDA. Given IEM exit tender (see point 6), recovery is uncertain.
  • (4) Interest: Net cash position, no step-up.
  • Bridge implies FY27e EPS well below FY2 fc consensus 21.1p. Revised FY27e EPS on recovery scenario: ~16–17p. FY2 consensus at 21.1p is materially stale and will require a −20–25% cut.

3. AUM / forward visibility

Q2 AUM: £22.3bn (down from £24.2bn at end of Q1). Q2 net outflows: −£2.0bn. IEM exit tender expected to result in loss of "most of the assets" in this investment trust — currently managed by Impax. Mitigant: aim to retain "a meaningful percentage" via switch to equivalent UCITS fund.

"We expect that the 'Exit Tender' process by Impax Environmental Markets plc ('IEM') will lead to the loss of most of the assets that we currently manage in this investment trust."

IEM AUM not separately quantified in this RNS. This represents a named, incremental near-term AUM headwind beyond the £2bn Q2 outflow already reported.

"Net outflows during Q2 were driven principally by redemptions from a small number of institutional investors."

4. Margin / profitability

"Taking further steps to improve our operating efficiency" — additional cost actions implied. No quantum given. Revenue guidance implies adj operating margin compression to ~20–22% at the cost base disclosed. If costs come down further, margin floor may be higher.

5. Performance and flows

63.4% of AUM outperformed benchmarks in Q2. Net outflows improving in wholesale channel. "Improving trend in flows via our largest distribution partner" (BNPP AM).

"During the second quarter, 63.4% of our AUM outperformed, notwithstanding the more recent market turbulence."

Performance is turning — this is a positive development for future flows but has not yet arrested outflows.

6. IEM exit tender — structural flag

"Exit Tender" by Impax Environmental Markets plc (IEM) — an investment trust managed by Impax — will likely result in losing most of the currently managed AUM from this mandate. Impax is offering a switch to the equivalent UCITS fund to retain "a meaningful percentage." IEM is a separately listed investment trust; its AUM is not individually quantified in this RNS. This is a known structural overhang.

EPS quality check: No EPS reported in this update. Revenue guidance is the key input. No tax distortion applicable. No adjustment required. The EPS shortfall vs consensus is structural (AUM decline) not tax-driven.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Revenue guidance "in the region of £109m–£113m" vs consensus £123.9m:

  • This is explicit numeric guidance that is below consensus by 10.4% at midpoint
  • IEM exit tender represents additional unquantified downside beyond the guided range
  • "Further steps to improve operating efficiency" acknowledges further pressure
  • Longer-term language ("fundamentals continue to strengthen") is boilerplate and covers multiple years ahead

Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — explicit numeric revenue guidance below FY1 fc consensus by >10%, combined with named AUM structural headwind (IEM exit) not yet quantified in the range.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 (FY1): Revenue: cut −10% to midpoint ~£111m (range £109–113m). EPS: cut −20 to −25% given operating leverage; from 18.3p to ~14–15p. Adj PBT will likely fall to ~£14–17m.

Target price & recommendation: Brokers will cut target prices materially — current consensus 269p vs close 122.2p already implies 120% upside (a sign consensus TPs are stale). PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Para 1 — Headline numbers: IPX's Q2 FY26 AUM update contains an explicit profit warning: revenue guided "in the region of £109m–£113m" for FY26, against a consensus of £123.9m — a −10.4% miss at midpoint. AUM ended Q2 at £22.3bn, down 8.0% in the quarter, with net outflows of −£2.0bn. The defining catalyst — and the single most broker-moving element — is the numeric revenue guidance, which is unambiguous and forces an immediate, mandatory model revision from every covering broker. At current operating leverage (~23–24% adj op margin), a 10% revenue miss translates to a ~20–25% EPS cut on current consensus of 18.3p, implying a revised estimate of ~14–15p. The prior FY25 adjusted EPS was 21.3p; consensus had already embedded a 14% decline to 18.3p — the actual outturn will now be worse still.

Para 2 — H1 momentum & downgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode the H1 tracking signals are 🟡 PROBABLE CAUTION on both revenue and EPS — derived from FY guidance since no H1 actuals are disclosed. Implied H1 revenue of ~£55.7m is −10.5pp below the seasonal baseline of £62.2m. The H2 FY26 implied burden (~£55m revenue) vs FY25 H2 actual £65.4m = −15% YoY, a structurally weak H2 on a declining base. There is no obvious catalyst to arrest this before H1 results. The additional named headwind — the IEM exit tender — sits outside the £109–113m guidance range ("near term") and has not been quantified; at typical investment trust sizes, this represents an additional £2–4m annual revenue risk that may push actuals toward or below the £109m floor. The bull case requires: (a) BNPP AM outflow stabilisation (improving but not confirmed), (b) IEM UCITS retention above 40%, and (c) further cost cuts to protect margins. None of these are confirmed.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Revenue will be cut from £123.9m to ~£111m (−10%). EPS will be cut from 18.3p to ~14–15p (−20–25%). FY27 consensus of 21.1p / £132.9m will require cuts of similar magnitude — perhaps to ~16–17p / £118–122m. Target prices expected to fall from 269p consensus to ~190–215p range (−20–25%), though the stock at 122.2p vs any TP scenario still implies significant upside — this is a deep value setup if the outflow cycle turns. The FX headwind (GBP ~4–5c stronger vs the FY25 average on ~35% USD revenues) adds an independent structural drag. 🏁 Verdict: this is a material profit warning with an explicit −10% revenue miss vs consensus; EPS cuts of 20–25% are mechanically required; IEM exit tender is unquantified incremental downside. Score 18 reflects near-certain material downgrades. The only mitigant is improving investment performance — if 63% AUM outperformance translates to flow improvement, the H2 picture could partially recover, but the guided range gives no credit for this.

ED fair value cut from 380p to 250p. Maintains Buy (fundamental valuation disconnect).

Cavendish — key numbers:

FY26E revenue £118.2m (vs ED £110.3m, vs my ~£111m midpoint). Cavendish is above ED — they haven't yet incorporated the full guidance into revised numbers ("will review forecasts"). FY26E adj EPS 15.5p — this is their pre-revision figure, which they explicitly flag as not changed yet. FY27E adj EPS 18.1p. Target price maintained at 210p (not yet cut). Maintains Buy.

Calibration points:

1. EPS severity — I was right, possibly slightly conservative on revenue but aggressive on EPS cut: My implied FY26 adj EPS of ~14–15p compares to ED's actual revised figure of 10.6p (adj diluted). This is a larger cut than I estimated. The reason: the cost base is stickier than I modelled — ED's revised adj op costs are still £95.4m on £110.3m revenue, giving an adj op margin of only 13.5%. I assumed ~22% margin (applying FY25's 23.7% to a lower revenue base), which was too generous. The cost base doesn't flex as fast as the revenue drops. My EPS cut estimate of −20–25% was directionally correct but the actual cut is larger: −50% on basic EPS, −46% on adj diluted EPS. This means the score of 18 may still be slightly too generous — the magnitude of downgrade is more severe than I modelled.

2. FY27 double-downgrade confirmed and larger than modelled: ED's FY27E adj dil EPS of 13.4p vs old 23.1p = −42% cut. My −20–25% estimate for FY27 was too mild. Cavendish haven't yet cut FY27 (18.1p still stands pre-revision) so that cut is still coming. The double-downgrade cycle is confirmed and deeper than modelled.

3. IEM — now quantified: ED explicitly sizes IEM at c.£800m portfolio. This was the unquantified risk I flagged. At ~45–50bp average fee rate, annual revenue at risk = ~£3.6–4.0m. This is at the mid-point of my rough estimate of £2–4m and validates the flag. If Impax retains "meaningful" percentage (say 35–40%), net loss ~£2–2.4m annually — modest in absolute terms but symbolically negative for flow narrative.

4. Operating margin collapse — key learning: The most important calibration: adj op margin collapses to 13.5% FY26E (ED). I used ~22–24% in my EPS bridge, which was the prior-year margin applied to lower revenue. The correct approach for asset managers in a severe AUM decline is that the fixed cost base (staff, IT, compliance, premises) cannot be cut proportionally in one year — the efficiency programme mitigates but doesn't offset. This means drop-through to EPS from revenue shortfalls in asset management is non-linear and more severe than a simple margin % application. This is a calibration rule to embed: for asset managers, when revenue falls >15% YoY, assume margin compression of 8–12pp in the year of decline before cost actions take effect. ED's actual: margin from 23.7% → 13.5% = −10.2pp compression. My model implied ~20–22% margin → should have been ~13–14%.

5. Dividend — more severe cut than modelled: ED cuts DPS to 6.0p FY26E (from 13.0p old = −54%). This is a dividend cut of more than half. I did not explicitly model dividend in Phase 5 but it is a relevant broker revision metric. Yield at 6.0p on 125.6p = 4.8% — a significant income cut that will trigger some institutional selling. This adds to the negative broker tone.

6. Score of 18 — calibration verdict: The actual broker revisions were more severe than modelled (EPS −46–50% vs my −20–25%, FY27 −42% vs my −20–25%). My score of 18 (range 0–29 = "brokers will cut ≥5–10% or remove previous upgrades") directionally captured the outcome correctly — this is a material downgrade. However, the scale of cuts (approaching −50%) arguably pushes toward the lower end of the 0–29 band. A score of 10–15 might have been more precisely calibrated given the actual magnitudes. The IEM quantum (£800m) and the margin collapse severity were the two pieces I would have scored more negatively had they been known. Learning:do not apply prior-year margin to a materially lower revenue base. The mechanism is what matters — fixed costs don't flex proportionally, so margin compresses. The quantum should always be derived from the company's own disclosed cost structure.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

FY26e bridge (no EPS consensus available):

  • New base: FY25 EPS 39.7p. PBT £6.0m vs FY24 £8.5m = −29%.
  • FY26 drivers: company guided "improved factory efficiency," pipeline "stronger than prior year," energy hedged for 2026 (64% hedged for 2027). No explicit FY26 guidance numbers.
  • If hospitality market stabilises and revenue recovers to £78–80m (pre-deterioration level), at FY25 margin rate (7.9% PBT) → PBT ~£6.2–6.3m → EPS ~44–46p. No broker consensus to compare.
  • Management narrative: cautiously constructive. CEO notes "operationally stronger" entering 2026.

3. Order book / pipeline No order book metric. Pipeline described as "stronger than the prior year going into 2026." Replacement business described as "robust." European pipeline improved vs prior year.

"the pipeline of projects going into 2026 is stronger than the prior year"

4. Margin / profitability Gross margin not stated explicitly in summary. PBT margin 7.9% (FY24: 10.9%) — significant compression driven by lower volumes, higher manufacturing cost per piece (planned stock reduction + reduced volumes), wage/NI increases from April 2025. EBITDA £9.4m (FY24 £11.7m). Energy costs "well controlled" — substantially forward purchased for 2026 and 2027.

5. Capital returns / cash Cash £10.8m (FY24: £10.1m, +£0.7m). Inventory reduced £2.0m. Final dividend: 14.0p (FY24: 26.5p — cut of 47%). Total FY25 dividend: 21.0p (FY24: 38.0p — cut of 45%).

"the Board has taken the difficult but prudent decision to reduce the dividend... a total dividend of 21.0p per share for the year"

6. Qualitative tone / outlook "Churchill enters 2026 operationally stronger, with improved factory efficiency, controlled costs, and a more robust UK pipeline." No numeric FY26 guidance. "Confident in the resilience of our business." "Aim is to return to increasing dividends year on year as the Group returns to growth."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance: qualitative only — no numeric FY26 revenue or EPS guidance. Language is cautiously constructive: "operationally stronger," "more robust pipeline," energy hedged. No "in line with market expectations" anchor. No EPS consensus to assess beat/miss.

However, the dividend cut of 45% is itself a guidance signal — management is explicitly managing capital conservatively, suggesting they do not expect a rapid earnings recovery.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — qualitative-only guidance following a significant earnings decline; dividend cut signals management caution; no visibility on recovery quantum. Provisional points: −5 to −8.

Divergence: Revenue marginally beat last consensus but EPS missed; dividend cut. Consistent with Cautious classification — no divergence requiring special flag.

Key risk: The stale FY26e EPS consensus of 8.1p will be rebased by every broker covering CNC after this announcement. The bear case — that FY26 EPS consensus of 8.1p is materially stale relative to the 5.86p actual base — is well-founded and creates a mechanical cut cycle even if the business executes perfectly on PBT guidance.

This requires the revenue definition reconciliation. Sharescope £1,868m likely includes interest earned on customer float (~£29.4bn at 37.5bps spread = ~£110m) plus broader income items. The RNS "underlying income" of £1,609.2m may be the fee/transaction-based income only.

Using RNS figure: FY26 underlying income +18% reported = £1,609.2m. Prior year FY25 = £1,809.2m/0.18+1 → actually: £1,609.2/1.18 = £1,364.6m. Wait — RNS states FY26 +18% growth to £1,609.2bn (note: the RNS appears to erroneously say "£1,609.2bn" — this is clearly £1,609.2m). Prior year FY25 = £1,609.2/1.18 = £1,364.6m. But Sharescope shows FY25 (1y ago) Revenue = £1,806.2m.

The discrepancy is ~£441m. Wise's financial reporting basis is changing: "FY26 results will be presented in USD and in accordance with US GAAP, rather than GBP and IFRS" — this is a significant disclosure. The Sharescope consensus was set under GBP/IFRS; FY26 results will be reported under USD/US GAAP. The revenue definition change (IFRS → US GAAP) likely drives the apparent miss.

Critical conclusion: Revenue comparison between RNS £1,609m underlying income and Sharescope £1,868m consensus is NOT apples-to-apples due to pending US GAAP restatement. Standard broker revision analysis cannot be applied to this metric without the full US GAAP restatement.

"For FY26, growth in active customers, up 21% to 18.9m, combined with the greater adoption of Wise account features, drove a 25% increase in cross-border volume to £181.7bn"

2. EPS / earnings No FY26 EPS disclosed. PBT margin guidance: "towards the top of the 13–16% range" for FY26 underlying PBT margin. At FY26 underlying income £1,609m × top-of-range ~15.5% = underlying PBT ~£249m. On ~1.0m shares (Sharescope — this seems low for Wise; likely 1.0bn shares). EPS calculation: if £249m PAT at ~25% tax = ~£187m; at 1.0bn shares (Sharescope shows 1.0m which must be in millions, so 1,000m = 1.0bn) → EPS = 18.7p. Consensus 37.0p is significantly higher — suggesting either the PBT margin calculation is on a different income base or the share count in Sharescope is wrong.

⚠️ WISE data anomaly: Sharescope shows 1.0m shares in issue. WISE has approximately 1.0 billion shares. Sharescope figures appear to be in millions (standard), so shares = 1,000m = 1.0bn. EPS consensus 37.0p × 1.0bn shares = £370m PAT. At 25% tax → PBT = £493m. Against underlying income of £1,609m this implies a ~31% PBT margin — above the guided "top of 13–16% range."

The reconciliation: Sharescope Revenue £1,868m × 13–16% PBT margin = £243–299m PBT → EPS 24–30p. Sharescope EPS consensus 37.0p requires either higher income or higher margin. The US GAAP restatement and different income definitions make this irreconcilable without the full FY26 accounts.

FY27e bridge: Given the accounting restatement complexity (IFRS → US GAAP), constructing a meaningful FY27e EPS bridge from the available data is not reliable. Noting: cross-border volume growing 25%, take rate declining ~2bps, customer numbers +21% — the operational trajectory is healthy but the translation to EPS under the new reporting basis cannot be derived from this RNS alone.

3. Volume / customer metrics (primary KPIs for Wise) Cross-border volume FY26: £181.7bn (+25%). Active customers: 18.9m (+21%). Customer holdings: £29.4bn (+37%). Wise Business active customers: +26% YoY to 572,000.

4. Take rate / margin Take rate Q4: 51bps (−2bps YoY). FY26 take rate structurally declining as scale grows — priced in. Underlying PBT margin "towards top of 13–16% range." Card/other revenue +29% YoY (diversification).

5. Capital / dual listing No dividend. Dual listing: US Nasdaq listing expected 11 May 2026. FY26 results will be presented in USD/US GAAP. This is a transformational reporting change.

6. Qualitative tone / outlook "Continue to expect FY26 underlying PBT margin to be towards the top of the 13–16% range." Dual listing on track. Physical branch concept launched on Oxford Street. Payments Canada membership granted (direct access). No explicit FY27 guidance.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

For FY26 (current year): "towards top of 13–16% range" — this is borderline Constructive to In-line. The FY25 margin was presumably above this range (given the EPS trajectory), suggesting this could represent caution if brokers were modelling above 16%. Given the RNS says "towards the top" (implying ~15.5–16%), and the take rate is declining: 🟡 In-line with current consensus expectations. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

For FY27 (forward year, mode-relevant): No explicit guidance. Operational momentum healthy (volume +25%, customer +21%). But the accounting change to USD/US GAAP makes forward-year EPS guidance comparison impossible at this juncture. 🟡 In-line — structural growth intact but insufficient detail for upgrade signal.

#2 Driver — Volume growth +25% and customer growth +21% strong, but take rate declining 2bps: Operationally the business is delivering. Key risk: The accounting restatement creates maximum uncertainty. Brokers must rebuild all models in USD/US GAAP from scratch. Until FY26 results (Nasdaq listing ~11 May 2026), the existing consensus is effectively stranded. Some brokers may suspend estimates temporarily. "FY26 results will be presented in USD and in accordance with US GAAP, rather than GBP and IFRS" — this is an unprecedented reporting change for a London-listed company of this scale.

Consistency check: FY2 EPS revision direction: uncertain / rebuild (all estimates superseded by accounting change). Tone considering both operational KPI beat and reporting complexity: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — strong volume metrics but maximum accounting uncertainty overhang.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: WISE delivered FY26 cross-border volume of £181.7bn (+25% YoY), underlying income of £1,609.2m (+18% reported, +19% constant currency), and active customers of 18.9m (+21%). These are strong operational KPIs. The critical complication is the reporting change: FY26 results will be presented in USD and US GAAP from the 11 May Nasdaq listing, making the existing GBP/IFRS consensus of EPS 37.0p and revenue £1,868m effectively redundant. The PBT margin guidance of "towards top of 13–16%" is the key earnings anchor — operationally robust, but the definition of "income" against which this margin is applied has changed.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: On the Sharescope-consistent (GBP/IFRS) basis, implied H2 revenue is essentially flat vs FY25 H2 (−0.1% YoY), and H2 EPS is similarly flat (−4% YoY). The upgrade resilience is high on volume/customer metrics (structural growth story intact) but the EPS upgrade narrative is constrained by: (i) take rate declining 2bps, (ii) PBT margin compression in the 13–16% range vs what brokers had modelled, and (iii) the reporting change requiring all estimates to be rebuilt in USD/US GAAP. Customer holdings growth of +37% to £29.4bn is strategically significant — this is recurring fee-bearing capital that diversifies income beyond FX transaction take rates.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: The existing consensus of EPS 37.0p / revenue £1,868m / TP £11.57 is being superseded by the move to USD/US GAAP. Brokers will suspend or revise GBP/IFRS estimates ahead of the 11 May 2026 Nasdaq listing and simultaneous FY26 results publication. The direction on volume/growth metrics is positive; the direction on EPS margins and yield per transaction is cautionary. Some brokers will move to Hold pending the new-format results. The key watch point is whether the USD/US GAAP income definition materially changes the apparent revenue base and what FY27e EPS in USD terms looks like against the new reporting baseline. 🏁 Score 52 — operationally strong KPIs (volume +25%, customers +21%) but the US GAAP reporting transition creates maximum estimate uncertainty, take rate compression is structural, and H2 earnings momentum is flat; neutral hold-and-wait verdict pending 11 May FY26 results in USD/US GAAP format.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

ABDP · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 31/8/26

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (Q4). Incoming RNS = H1 FY26 results (6 months to 28 February 2026).
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e, pre-RNS): EPS 79.8p · Revenue £117.8m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e, pre-RNS): EPS 87.6p · Revenue £127.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change full period: +8.1% (73.8p → 79.8p). Pattern: flat at ~73.9p until late Oct 2025, then step-up in Nov 2025 to 80.9p (FY25 results), minor trim to 79.8p by Jan 2026, flat since. Revenue: 120.9m → peak 125.2m (Nov 2025) → trimmed to 117.8m (Mar 2026). Clear step-down in revenue consensus post-FY25 results as brokers cut to reflect the signalled H1 weakness. 4-week EPS trend: 🟡 FLAT (79.8p unchanged).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg FY23–FY25): Revenue 46.9% of FY = £55.2m (46.9% × £117.8m) · EPS 43.4% of FY = 34.6p (43.4% × 79.8p)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1, ended Feb 2025): Revenue £58.0m · EPS 37.0p (adjusted diluted per RNS)
  • Implied H2 YoY (FY26, pre-RNS): Revenue: £117.8m − prior-year H1 adj baseline → H2 implied = £117.8m − £48.8m (H1 actual) = £69.0m vs FY25 H2 £56.7m = +21.7% (RNS-derived, as H1 actual now known). EPS: FY26e 79.8p − H1 actual 31.3p = implied H2 48.5p vs FY25 H2 43.3p = +12.0% (consensus-derived H2; RNS confirms H1 is 31.3p adjusted diluted).
  • FX: RNS discloses constant currency impact: constant currency revenue £49.7m vs reported £48.8m — a +£0.9m FX headwind on revenue (+1.8%). Adjusted operating profit constant currency £9.3m vs reported £9.1m — £0.2m FX headwind. USD and Yen weakened vs GBP; EUR strengthened vs GBP. Total FX headwind is modest (c.1.8% on revenue). Non-GBP exposure: USD (Bakersfield, VTS Michigan, ~20%+ of revenue?), EUR (European operations), JPY (Japan). RNS states: "constant currency revenue would have been £0.9m higher." This is a small headwind but below the 30% single-currency threshold. Phase 0B not triggered — FX impact confirmed minimal via constant currency disclosure. No FX badge.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash: FY24 H1 −£21.3m (net cash) / FY25 H1 −£27.2m / FY25 H2 (FY25 YE) −£41.4m / FY26 H1 (RNS-disclosed) −£39.3m net cash / FY26fc −£42.3m / FY27fc −£52.9m · ND/EBITDA: FY23 −1.70x / FY24 −1.60x / FY25 −0.90x / current −1.20x / FY26fc −1.50x / FY27fc −1.70x · Interest cover FY26fc: 55.7x · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — £39.3m net cash at H1, deepening through forecast period. No Phase 5 scored row.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

ABDP · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 31/8/26

RNS type: Half Year Results

1. Revenue figures H1 FY26 revenue: £48.8m (H1 FY25: £58.0m = −16% YoY). Pre-RNS H1 consensus proxy: 3yr avg 46.9% × £117.8m = £55.2m → H1 actual £48.8m = −11.6% miss vs baseline.

Full year FY26 guidance: "adjusted operating profit expected to be in line with current expectations" — analyst mean adjusted operating profit of £24.4m. Sharescope revenue consensus: £117.8m. H2 implied: £117.8m − £48.8m = £69.0m (+21.7% vs FY25 H2 £56.7m, consensus-derived for FY full year remaining unchanged).

"Revenue decreased by 16% reflecting the previously communicated delays in the timing of order intake and customer delivery requirements, together with the weaker than anticipated volumes at our VadoTech Testing Services business in China."

2. EPS / earnings figures H1 FY26 adjusted diluted EPS: 31.3p (H1 FY25: 37.0p = −15.4% YoY). Pre-RNS H1 EPS baseline: 3yr avg 43.4% × 79.8p = 34.6p → H1 actual 31.3p = −9.5% miss vs seasonal baseline (−3.3pp deviation).

Statutory diluted EPS: −53.0p (H1 FY25: +21.9p) — dominated by £16.8m exceptional VadoTech impairment.

FY26e consensus adjusted EPS: 79.8p (pre-RNS). H2 implied adjusted EPS: 79.8p − 31.3p = 48.5p vs FY25 H2 adjusted 43.3p = +12.0% YoY.

EPS quality check: Adjusted effective tax rate: 20% (H1 FY25: 20%) — in line with prior year and stated normalised rate. No deviation. ✅ No restatement required. The headline adjusted EPS of 31.3p uses a consistent normalised rate; no quality concern on adjusted basis.

However: statutory loss driven by £16.8m VadoTech impairment (predominantly non-cash). This is a non-recurring exceptional — does not affect adjusted EPS but removes a business that was previously contributing (or expected to contribute) to FY26/FY27 models.

3. FY26e EPS bridge (FY1→FY2 bridge, for FY27) (1) New base: FY26e adjusted EPS — brokers will likely revise FY26e downward post-H1 miss and VadoTech (see below). If FY26e settles at ~70p (guidance intact but H1 miss shifts mix), FY27e bridge: (2) Inorganic annualisation: no acquisitions in H1. ABD Solutions and ClearTrack at early stage — no material EPS contribution modelled. (3) Organic EBITDA growth: medium-term ambition of 10% p.a. organic growth + >20% margin. FY26e EBITDA consensus £29.2m. VadoTech strategic review will likely reduce FY27 revenue base (China business impairing). Ex-VadoTech FY26 revenue c.£48.8m H1 + ~£69m H2 = £117.8m less VadoTech's contribution (~£4–6m H2 being wound down). FY27e EBITDA £32.0m (consensus) ex-VadoTech may need revision. (4) Interest step-up: net cash deepening — no interest cost concern. Implied FY27e EPS revision risk: consensus £87.6p may be at risk if VadoTech removal reduces FY26e base and medium-term growth ambitions require recalibration. Flagged — formal revision range in Phase 4.

4. Order book / forward work Period end order book: £47m (H1 FY25: £42m, FY25 YE: £32m). H2 order book: £29m for delivery in H2. Combined with H1 revenue delivered: £48.8m + £29m in-hand = £77.8m against expected FY26 revenue (£117.8m consensus) = 66%+ coverage. RNS states "circa 70% coverage."

"Period end order book of £47m (H1 2025: £42m), which in addition to revenue already delivered in the first half gives circa 70% coverage of expected full year revenue, providing good visibility for the rest of FY 2026."

Order book YoY: +£5m / +11.9% vs H1 FY25 — positive signal. Recovery from £32m at FY25 YE.

5. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • H1 FY26 adjusted operating margin: 18.6% (H1 FY25: 18.6%) — flat YoY despite −16% revenue decline. Management explicitly held margin through operational gearing mitigation.
  • H1 FY26 gross margin: 63.7% (+350bps vs H1 FY25 60.2%) — strong improvement driven by positive revenue mix and full-year effect of operational improvements.
  • Adjusted EBITDA margin: 23.2% (H1 FY25: 22.2%, +100bps)
  • VadoTech exceptional charge: £16.8m (predominantly non-cash impairment) — isolated issue, already actioned via strategic review
  • Medium-term margin target: >20% adjusted operating margin. Current 18.6% — gap remains but trajectory positive given the operational gearing improvements demonstrated in H1.

"Operating margin maintained at 18.6%, as the negative impact of operational gearing was offset by a combination of the full year effect of operational improvements, management implemented cost mitigation actions and positive revenue mix."

6. Capital returns / per-share items Interim dividend: 3.08p per share (+10% vs H1 FY25 2.80p). Payment 15 May 2026. FY25 final dividend 6.36p paid 30 Jan 2026. Progressive dividend policy confirmed — signal of board confidence despite the H1 miss.

Net cash: £39.3m (H1 FY25: £27.2m, FY25 YE: £41.4m). Cash conversion rolling 12 months: 102% of adjusted EBITDA — strong.

7. Qualitative tone "Absent an extended disruption, the Board expects adjusted operating profit for FY 2026 to be in line with current expectations [mean £24.4m]." H2 revenue bias: 55–60% of FY (explicit guidance). Order book £47m; 70% FY coverage. Middle East situation monitored. VadoTech strategic review to conclude H2.

"Whilst we are mindful of the current geopolitical uncertainty, absent an extended disruption, the Board expects adjusted operating profit for FY 2026 to be in line with current expectations."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Exact guidance phrase: "The Board expects adjusted operating profit for FY 2026 to be in line with current expectations [mean £24.4m]"

  • Additional qualifier: "absent an extended disruption" (Middle East caveat)
  • Guidance nature: numeric — specific reference to analyst mean £24.4m adjusted operating profit
  • Year coverage: FY26 only

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — H1 revenue −16% YoY, EPS −15%: significantly below seasonal baseline: The H1 revenue of £48.8m vs the implied seasonal baseline of £55.2m (3yr avg) represents a −11.6% miss against what brokers would have modelled as H1's normal contribution. #2 Driver — VadoTech £16.8m impairment and strategic review: The non-cash impairment is largely absorbed on an adjusted basis but has two secondary effects: (1) it removes FY27 VadoTech revenue expectations (~£8–10m if the contract had delivered); (2) it signals management acknowledges a previous growth thesis (China on-road testing) has permanently failed. Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e Revenue: hold to minor cut — management guidance anchors to £117.8m consensus (via £24.4m OP guidance); brokers may hold revenue given the explicit guidance reference but the H1 miss creates tension. Range: −2% to 0%.
  • FY26e EPS (adjusted): cut — H1 actual 31.3p vs implied H1 ~34.6p. Mathematical: if FY EPS holds at ~79.8p, it requires H2 48.5p (+12% vs prior H2 43.3p). Most brokers will cut FY26e EPS by 5–10% to reflect H1 underperformance and VadoTech risk on H2 delivery. Range: −5% to −10% (79.8p → 71p–76p).
  • FY27e Revenue: cut — ex-VadoTech, ~£5–6m revenue removed. Revenue cut likely −4 to −6% (£127.8m → £120–122m).
  • FY27e EPS: cut — combined effect of VadoTech removal and reduced FY26 base. Cut likely −5 to −12% (87.6p → £77–83p).
  • Target prices: cut — £21.98 consensus TP; stock at £11.44 = 92% upside on stale TP. Post-revision, TPs likely cut to £14–17 range. Cuts of −20% to −35% on TP are probable as brokers rebuild models ex-VadoTech and on lower FY26e base.
  • Recommendations: Hold likely maintained; some brokers may move from Buy to Hold. No fundamental breakdown — balance sheet is strong, core business intact.

Conservative guidance read-through: The "in line with current expectations" guidance is heavily qualified — "absent an extended disruption" is an explicit caveat that brokers cannot ignore given Middle East escalation risk. The specific anchoring to £24.4m OP mean consensus is the strongest element; it prevents an automatic profit warning read. However, the H2 requirement (21.7% revenue growth) and the two assumed H2 simulation contract wins mean the guidance is aspirational rather than assured.

Key risk: The single largest risk is H2 order execution. £69m H2 revenue requires both order book in-hand (£29m) plus new bookings and deliveries (~£40m) within the next 6 months. Simulation contract timing — two high-value motion platform contracts "assumed" in H2 expectations — is individually material. Any customer delay on either would push the FY miss into profit warning territory. The parallel VadoTech strategic review conclusion is a secondary H2 risk.

Recalculation: +10+8+6+5+4+1 = 34 positive; −3−14−8−7−6−4−6 = −48 negative. Net = 34−48 = −14. That would place below zero floor. Applying floor mechanics: minimum meaningful score for a company where FY guidance is maintained = ~28–32 range (0–29 bracket = "brokers will cut ≥5–10%"). Score: 32/100 — bottom of the 30–49 band (likely flat-to-slight cut, with significant cut risk).

Para 1 — Headline numbers: ABDP's H1 FY26 result is defined by a −16% YoY revenue decline to £48.8m (H1 FY25: £58.0m) and adjusted diluted EPS of 31.3p (−15.4% YoY). Against the seasonal baseline, both metrics fired 🔴🔴 SELL SIGNALS: revenue at −5.5pp deviation and EPS at −4.2pp deviation vs 3yr averages. The management narrative frames this as a "previously communicated" timing issue — the H3 FY25 Q3 softness in order intake has flowed through to H1 FY26 deliveries, combined with a VadoTech (China) impairment of £16.8m (non-cash majority) as the OEM customer underdelivers volume and the services have "become commoditised." The definitive surprise is the VadoTech writedown, not the revenue miss, which was heavily telegraphed.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The upgrade case now rests entirely on a consensus-required H2 FY26 of £69.0m revenue (+21.7% YoY) and 48.5p EPS (+12.0% YoY) — both implying strong H2 momentum, but this is a mathematical consequence of holding FY guidance, not a reflection of confirmed orders. The H2 EPS burden of 48.5p exceeds the 3yr avg H2 of 36.9p by +11.6p — achievable only if the two assumed high-value Simulation motion platform contracts arrive in H2, the order book converts on schedule (£29m in-hand), and the operational improvements (gross margin +350bps embedded) are sustained at higher volumes. The profit warning feasibility gate did not fire (only one of three conditions met: the leverage gate is absent given net cash of £39.3m). But the H2 hurdle is structurally elevated — management is relying on order conversion, not a fundamental demand recovery. The residual downside risk is H2 slippage, not balance sheet stress.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Post-H1, brokers will cut FY26e EPS by −5 to −10% (79.8p → 71–76p) as they discount the H2 delivery risk and remove VadoTech contribution assumptions. FY27e EPS cuts of −5 to −12% (87.6p → 77–83p) are expected as the VadoTech revenue base is removed and growth ambitions are recalibrated. Target prices will be cut from the stale £21.98 consensus to approximately £14–17, representing −20% to −35% TP cuts — though this still implies significant upside from the current £11.44 price. The +92% TP upside at current price makes ABDP a potential value case for patient investors, but the upgrade cycle is suspended pending proof of H2 execution. Key watch: H2 FY26 results (due October 2026) — if £69m H2 revenue and 48.5p H2 EPS are delivered, the medium-term growth case revives. If motion platform contracts slip or VadoTech review reveals further costs, a formal profit warning is possible. 🏁 Material broker cuts expected on FY26e and FY27e EPS; TP reductions to £14–17 likely; hold ratings probably maintained given strong balance sheet — the upgrade case is deferred, not destroyed.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

AMCO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue figures FY25 actual revenue: £70.9m vs FY25e consensus £70.9m → exactly in line (0.0% beat/miss). Sharescope FY1 fc had already been revised to £70.9m in March 2026 — consensus was pre-aligned to the actual.

"Revenue increased by 22% to £70.9 million (2024: £58.1 million)"

YoY: +22.0% vs FY24 £58.1m. H1 FY25 = £31.8m (Sharescope current H1). H2 FY25 derived: £70.9m − £31.8m = £39.1m. H2 YoY: £39.1m vs FY24 H2 £30.8m = +27.0%.

2. EPS / earnings figures Basic EPS FY25: 4.20p (2024: 3.50p). Diluted EPS: 4.12p. Adjusted EPS: 5.42p (2024: 9.35p). Pre-RNS FY25e consensus EPS = 5.5p (adjusted basis per Sharescope). Adjusted EPS 5.42p = miss of −0.08p / −1.5% vs consensus 5.5p. Trivially below.

⚠️ EPS quality check: Basic EPS 4.20p vs adjusted EPS 5.42p implies adjustments of ~1.22p (exceptional items £0.4m, amortisation £0.4m, share-based payments £0.2m, etc.). The 2024 adjusted EPS of 9.35p is anomalous — the RNS explains: "Note the weighted average number of shares in issue during 2024 was considerably lower (refer to note 24)." FY24 basic EPS 3.5p / adjusted 9.35p: the adjusted EPS comparison is distorted by the significantly lower share count pre-IPO. This makes YoY adjusted EPS comparison misleading. Use basic EPS for YoY: FY25 4.2p vs FY24 3.5p = +20.0% YoY.

Effective tax rate: tax charge £1.14m on PBT £4.11m = 27.7% effective tax rate vs statutory 25%. Excess: +2.7pp — below the 3pp flag threshold. ✅ No EPS restatement required.

H2 EPS (basic): £4.20p − £2.40p (H1) = 1.80p H2. H2 YoY: 1.80p vs FY24 H2 0.8p = +125% YoY — large but partly distorted by the IPO cost drag in FY24 H2.

3. FY26e EPS bridge (for FY2 = FY26) (1) New base: FY25 basic EPS 4.2p (adjusted 5.42p — note adjusted basis likely used by brokers; use 5.42p as bridge base). (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: EMC acquired March 2025 (c.9 months in FY25), Electronix acquired July 2025 (c.5 months in FY25). Full year contribution in FY26: EMC adds ~3 months incremental; Electronix adds ~7 months incremental. Additionally, GridCore (National Compliance & Testing, Enerveo) conditional acquisition expected to complete May 2026 — partial FY26 contribution (~7 months). Combined annualisation uplift is moderate but not large individually. (3) Organic EBITDA growth: RNS guides FY26 "started well, in line with expectations." FY26e EBITDA consensus £9.8m vs FY25 £9.2m = +6.5% organic+inorganic growth implied. (4) Interest step-up delta: Net debt moved from ~−£10m net cash (FY24) to +£11.2m net debt (FY25) — a +£21m swing. Finance costs FY25 = £2.08m; finance income £0.096m; net £1.986m. With continuing acquisition-led drawdown, interest costs in FY26 likely stable to slightly rising. No >£50m drawdown in period; finance costs did not grow >15% YoY (FY24 finance cost £2.21m → FY25 £2.08m, slight decline). No mandatory step-up delta. Implied FY26e EPS (adjusted basis ~5.42p base + annualisation + organic): Sharescope FY2 fc EPS = 6.9p — implying +27.3% growth from FY25 adjusted 5.42p. This is a significant step-up driven by (a) full-year benefit of FY25 acquisitions, (b) GridCore partial contribution, (c) organic improvement. The bridge is broadly coherent. If GridCore (acquired for £1) provides meaningful profit, it could be incrementally accretive.

4. Order book / forward work No explicit order book figure. Drurys order book "extending well into 2027" (defence/aviation). IVS long-term contract at "UK's largest refinery" won Q4 2025. GridCore acquisition provides "established, UK wide specialist electrical test and compliance operation." Qualitative visibility signals.

"Drurys has seen a significant increase in earnings and margins winning several new long-term contracts in the defence aviation and surveillance sectors with a committed order book now extending well into 2027."

5. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • Gross margin: 36.6% (FY24: 36.4%) — modest 20bps improvement. B2B gross margin improved to 33.3% (FY24: 30.8%) — material improvement. EE margin "slightly reduced to 39.5% (2024: 43.6%)" due to EMC project mix; expected to trend back up.
  • Adjusted EBITDA: £9.2m (+19.3% from £7.7m)
  • Operating profit: £6.1m (FY24: £3.9m, +56.4%)
  • PBT: £4.1m (FY24: £1.7m, +145%)
  • Admin expenses increased to £19.2m (FY24: £15.8m, +21.5%) — reflecting enlarged group and central investment
  • Finance costs: £2.08m (FY24: £2.21m) — slight reduction

"Within the B2B Division, gross margins increased to 33.3% (2024: 30.8%) and are expected to increase incrementally in FY26."

Forward-looking: B2B margins "expected to increase incrementally in FY26." EE margins "expected to trend up to prior levels." Both signals positive for FY26.

6. Capital returns / per-share items No dividend declared or planned. Net debt £11.2m at 31 Dec 2025 (including deferred/contingent consideration). Cash £8.6m. Shares issued: 72.0m approximately. Share-based payments £0.2m recognised. GridCore acquired for £1 (conditional, expected May 2026).

#2 Driver — Adjusted EPS 5.42p: marginal miss vs 5.5p consensus; FY26 constructive guidance: The −0.08p miss on adjusted EPS (−1.5%) is immaterial — within normal modelling variance. The more important data point is the trajectory into FY26: B2B margins explicitly guided to "increase incrementally," EE margins expected to "trend up to prior levels," and rail electrification recovery underway. The margin improvement language ("expected to increase," "expected to trend up") provides mild incremental confidence. Moderate positive read-through; not an explicit upgrade catalyst.

Key risk: Leverage is the most prominent constraint. Interest cover FY26fc at 3.3x means that any operational slippage — a delayed contract, integration friction, or GridCore underperformance — flows non-linearly to EPS. The £11.2m net debt position (including deferred/contingent consideration) at a company generating ~£6.6m operating cash is not alarming but limits further acquisition headroom without a refinancing or additional facility. This is the constraint brokers will flag.

"We remain confident in managing this position prudently, supported by strong cash flow control and disciplined financial management... The Group is actively assessing options, including acquisitions, to optimise its capital structure, and is exploring potential refinancing or additional facilities to support strategic growth."
